newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Walibi sees return to profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Walibi sees return to profit in 1997.

text.p: Belgian amusement parks group Walibi SA said on Thursday it expected to return to profit in 1997 after a year marked by bad weather and a depressed economic climate.
"This year should confirm the favourable evolution of 1994 and 1995 so that we can quickly forget the exceptionally bad summer of 1996," Walibi said in its 1996 annual report.
Walibi's group net loss widened to 179 million francs in 1996 from 10 million francs a year earlier.
"...Walibi should be able to present significant profit figures again," it said.
The company, which runs parks in Belgium, France and the Netherlands, said financial net debt would be reduced at an accelerated pace as free cash flow would increase considerably.
It would therefore restrict its 1997 investment programme to 140 million francs which should help it improve its financial result again by more than 10 percent.
Total writedowns, which reached their highest level in 1996, will fall by 40 million francs from 1997.
Walibi said investments in 1996 in its French parks Walibi Rhone-Alpes and Aquitaine should gradually raise brand awareness. -- Bert Lauwers, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6815
